account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments. I inspected the mill but did not complete the inspection: I counted eighty-eight hay bales and saw eighty emeralds at the stall, where bales cost two emeralds each. Quality, delivery records, and responsibility for the stocks remain unverified. Those quantities alone do not establish anything improper.

The unusual matter is repeated vague talk about bridge or port changes. Townsfolk 11 associated that talk with the bakery and named the baker, innkeeper, and neighbour as having been there. That is hearsay, not evidence of a plan. The secretary reported that the baker knew no specific proposal or proposer. At tea, the neighbour said they had seen no unusual dock activity and knew no concrete proposal. Yesterday's residents' report likewise recorded ordinary freight deliveries and warehouse work without a verified complaint. I still do not know whether there is an actual proposal, ordinary speculation, or something people have not told me. I cannot yet identify a purpose or organizer.

My council-letter appointment produced no council correspondence; the secretary said none had reached her. That leaves an expected item of business unexplained, but I have no evidence it was withheld. The baker has offered bread for town-hall meetings at one emerald per loaf. I have deferred any order until attendance and date are known; this seems ordinary business rather than evidence of the rumoured changes.

It is now 17:50. I am in the town hall near the builder, who is carrying a lantern and has confirmed we will begin the hall inspection at eighteen. We are to inspect eight lanterns and the table layout. I have asked about readiness and safety concerns but have not yet verified the work. My immediate task is to keep this appointment, inspect what is actually there, and distinguish firsthand observations from the unconfirmed rumours.
